slides.title: Five brief mistakes that *quietly burn* creator budget.
slides.subtitle: From 850+ creator deals. None look expensive until the reshoot.

slides.label: 01 · Writing their script
slides.title: You hired a voice, then muted it.
slides.body: A word-for-word script makes a creator sound like an ad. Their audience scrolls. Give them *the one thing to get across* and let them say it their way.

slides.label: 02 · Six key messages
slides.title: If everything matters, nothing lands.
slides.body: A 30-second video can carry one message, maybe two. Pick the one that matters. The rest goes on the landing page, not in the creator's mouth.

slides.label: 03 · No approved claims
slides.title: Vague claims mean late rewrites.
slides.body: If the brief doesn't list exactly what can be said about the product, legal finds out at draft stage. That's when changes cost the most. List the *approved claims* up front.

slides.label: 04 · Feedback from everyone
slides.title: Four reviewers, four directions.
slides.body: When nobody owns approval, the creator gets contradicting notes and a third round. Name one approver and *cap feedback at two rounds* in the brief.

slides.label: 05 · Hiding the real plan
slides.title: Say if it'll run as an ad.
slides.body: Creators film differently for paid use: clean hooks, cutdowns, no time-bound jokes. Hide that, and you pay again for edits. Put *usage and the real KPI* in the brief.
